card.title: How To Fix an iPhone 8 With No Image. Turns on but nothing shows on the screen

source.title: How To Fix an iPhone 8 With No Image. Turns on but nothing shows on the screen

claims.statement: On iPhone 8 / 8 Plus no-image, the most common fault is pry damage to filter FL5705 (240 Ω, 0201) at LCD connector J5700; replacing it usually fixes it.
Other J5700 faults: PP5V7_DISPLAY_AVDDH_CONN, PP5V7_MESON_AVDDH_CONN or PN5V7_DISPLAY_MESON_AVDDN_CONN shorted; good lines read about 200–700 mV in diode mode. Inject only 2–3 V (max 5.7 V).
If the connector reads fine, check Chestnut U5600: C5600 must have no continuity across it; check for corrosion under U5600, then replace it.

procedure: Rule out screen, DFU and backlight-only faults.
Diode-check J5700; inspect and replace FL5705.
Find shorts on AVDDH/AVDDN lines with 2–3 V injection.
Check FL3906 if PP1V8_LCM_CONN is OL.
Check C5600 and under U5600; replace U5600.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
